The moons shone from the night sky. Jiu Xing was all prepared to leave before the Chloran Army made their final trek before finishing off the Flora. She hopped on Stone and set off for where the Flora were supposed to be living.

Jiu passed countless lands, forests, plains, mountains, yet no Flora was to be found. She was quite confused, they were supposed to be here after all, weren't they? That's when she heard a scream, no two screams. Following where it came from she was led into a cave, where a sight caught her full attention.

A creature that looked like a Chlora but smaller was laying against the cave wall. Was this what a Flora was? Jiu didn't question much, as she noticed something odd, a pool of red liquid. She ran over to the Flora, and held its head up. It was an older creature, with stab wounds all over her body. She began speaking as best she could to Jiu.

"Hhheher... tttatakee hher... pppleplease." The Flora tried her best to speak, but was clearly in pain

Take her? There was no one else here besides the bleeding out Flora. That's when she heard the second scream from before. Covered in blood in the Flora's lap was a baby Flora, with its cord still attached. Jiu took cord, cut it, and picked the baby up and cleaned it off as best she could, checking to see if there were any wounds. Luckily there were none.

Jiu asked the Flora which seemed to be the baby's mother, "Where is everyone? Where were the other Flora? What happened?"

The mother let out a scream, in turn having the baby begin crying again, "Gggone... pppoof... llleft... al...alone."

"Hold on, I'll help you so you won't be in pain"

Yet the mother didn't respond. Her breathing began to slow down. Her eyes lost their color. She had died.

The cave fell silent. No screams, no baby crying, nothing. Jiu now realized what had happened, that the Flora were no longer here, that the baby may be the last remaining Flora around. She had to change the Chlora's minds about the Flora, to protect the baby from harm.

She walked out of the cave into pouring rain. Around her she could now see the huts that the Flora had lived in, all deserted, empty. She entered each house looking for supplies that she may need. She came across countless things, toys that were in the middle ofbeing played with, food half eaten, homes with fire pits still lit. She also came across various footprints. Children's prints, prints of a Lot'dy, and the prints of those that seemed to just end in the middle of no path.

----------

After she gathered all she needed, she waited for the Chloran Army to arrive to see what was left. As the soldiers entered the village, they noticed Jiu. Commander Hua Bing walked up to Jiu and questioned her.

"Child, what are you doing here? It's dangerous out here with these savages about!"

Jiu looked up at the soldier, "Perhaps it was before, but after being here for a while, I've realized it isn't"

"What do you mean? Are there no Flora in the place?"

"Yes, all of them have vanished. The only one that remains is this child, whose mother passed before my very eyes."

"You went up to them? That's insanely dangerous, you could've been killed!"

"I couldn't've been killed, for she was already on the path to the afterlife. And in the time I spent with her as she was dying, she cared not for trying to kill me, not for drawing patterns, but for her child, to make sure she was safe."

"Child, you know you aren't allowed out here. Why did you come?"

"I knew that the Flora were good, I needed to prove to you that they were. There was no reason to kill them."

"There was ample reason. Our goddess Yuna had told us to, for they were a plague upon Gaea"

"How do you know Yuna said that? You only listened to the High Priestess. For all you know she could be lying to you."

"The High Priestess has never been wrong before. There is no way she could've been wrong this time.

"But she was, she was wrong about the Flora!"

"Silence! I won't have you speak against the High Priestess and Yuna. They would never betray us!"

"But they did! They did betray you!"

Hua Bing pulled out a spear and pointed it directly at Jiu. "Child, I told you to be quiet. As of your arrival here, you cast suspicion upon yourself. You holding that Flora and trying to have me consider them innocent is going against Yuna's orders. For that, you will have to pay with your life."

Hua Bing raised his spear in the air, readying a downwards thrust straight into Jiu, when all of a sudden, a spear protruded straight out of his gut. One after another, spears began poking out of him, pinning him in place. A group of soldier walked in front of Hua Bing and began talking.

"Commander, I'm sorry we had to do this, but we believe the child ourselves. We've rummaged through the homes looking for any Flora and none were to be found. The only one we had seen was the mother in the cave, who is no longer apart of this world. Everywhere we looked we found no markings, besides in books that detailed Floran history and culture."

"You men can't be serious," Hua Bing began to laugh, "You are directly disobeying Yuna, and have wounded one of your own brethren."

"I'm sorry commander, but I'm afraid we are serious. Please forgive us."

Hua Bing started laughing uncontrollably, until his laughter began to fade, and stopped for good. He had died.

The soldiers turned to Jiu "Child what is your name?"

"Jiu. Jiu Xing."

"Okay Jiu, let's head back to the Tree of Life and declare what has happened and what we now know."

"How will the Flora child be?"

"The Flora are no longer a threat to us. As for the child, it will need a parent, and seeing as you were the one to take care it after the mother died, you can become the mother if you want."

"I would love to, thank you"

"Certainly"

----------

The Chloran Army arrived back at the Tree of Life with Jiu, Stone, and the Flora Child. The Army spread the news of what they had witnessed, and how the commander was reacting. The Chlora took the news happily, and welcomed their peace with the Flora. As for the High Priestess, she had been put on trial, and had been found guilty of making up several times or changing what Yuna had said. Jiu became a happy mother to the Flora, yet was still not over what had happened to them. She desperately wanted to know where they were and what had happened to them.
